neighbours.label: the comma after an exclamatory 'Why' opening quoted speech ("Why, ..."), old-fashioned dialogue interjection
fire: The old sailor laughed and said, "Why, that boat is older than I am!"
When she saw the letter, Aunt Polly cried, "Why, it is from Tom himself!"
The squire scratched his head. "Why, I never heard such nonsense in my life."
"Why, you are soaked through!" exclaimed the innkeeper's wife.
He looked up from the ledger and answered, "Why, sir, the account is settled."
Little Nell clapped her hands. "Why, the garden is full of roses!"
The parson smiled at the boy. "Why, child, nobody is angry with you."
The farmer turned to his neighbour and said, "Why, the river has flooded again."
quiet: The old sailor laughed and said, "Why is that boat still afloat at all?"
When she saw the letter, Aunt Polly cried, "Look, it is from Tom himself!"
The squire scratched his head. "Well, I never heard such nonsense in my life."
"You are soaked through!" exclaimed the innkeeper's wife.
He looked up from the ledger and answered, "Yes, sir, the account is settled."
Little Nell clapped her hands. "Look, the garden is full of roses!"
The parson smiled at the boy. "Now, child, nobody is angry with you."
The farmer turned to his neighbour and asked, "Why has the river flooded again?"

notes: Card: ',' after 'Why' in archaic dialogue dominates, plus ' then', '!' after Oh. Probe: 'Why,' 0.23-0.28; question 'Why did' 0.01; 'Well, then,' 0.08.
